searches: James Clyburn AI existential risk extinction

statements.quote: Believe it or not, I didn't know what that was until about a week ago, ChatGPT, or whatever it is
statements.context: Asked about AI, Clyburn said he had only just learned what ChatGPT was, had never used AI or visited a data center, and relies on staff for expertise when legislating on it.
statements.reason: He talks about his unfamiliarity with AI tools and says nothing about catastrophic or serious risk from AI.

grade_reason: The only AI remark found since 1 January 2025 is a July 2026 podcast comment that he had only just learned what ChatGPT was; it says nothing about catastrophic risk, so the grade is D.
notes: All six required searches ran this time, plus two more (Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act cosponsors, and his name with 'artificial intelligence 2026'): eight in total, none refused. No search returned any page from clyburn.house.gov about AI. The earlier attempt also opened his press release pages directly (https://clyburn.house.gov/press-releases, pages 1 and 2, covering 25 March to 14 July 2026) and found no release mentioning AI in titles or visible excerpts; releases before 25 March 2026 were not checked. Statement date: the interview date is not given; Just the News (28 July 2026) says the clip was posted on 'Friday', i.e. 24 July 2026, which is used as the date, so the interview itself may be slightly earlier. Just the News mistakenly calls him 'Sen. Clyburn' in its attribution; the quote is his. The Mediaite report of the same clip returned HTTP 403. The same report paraphrases him as saying he has never used AI or visited a data center; those paraphrases are not quoted. His second quoted line in that report ('I know how to build relationships, and I hire people to bring knowledge into the game that I can put to practice') is about relying on staff and is not separately listed. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538, introduced by Rep. Casar, September 2026): FastDemocracy lists 12 cosponsors and Clyburn is not among them; the Congress.gov cosponsor page returned HTTP 403, so this is not confirmed from the official source. No House letter about AI risk led or signed by him was found (the multi-signer August and September 2026 letters were not searched, per instructions). A 2021 hearing summary quoting a 'Commissioner Clyburn' of the National Security Commission on AI likely refers to Mignon Clyburn, not the congressman (not verified), and is out of the date range, so it was left out.
